To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the corrosion rate in the nanocomposite coating is directly proportional to surface stress, surface modulus, surface poro-elasticity and permeability, and inversely proportional to surface elastic modulus and grain size.
the corrosion behavior of nanocomposite coating can be analyzed by incorporating the effects of surface stress, surface elasticity, surface porosity as well as the permeability of the nanocoating.
surface stress, surface permeability and surface porosity are the main mechanical factors affecting the corrosion behavior of nanocomposite materials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a set of equations for the corrosion failure of the nanocomposite coating.
the effects of intrinsic parameters on the corrosion behavior of nanocomposite materials.
the study of the effects of mechanical parameters on electrochemical reactions in the nanocomposite coating.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the surface stress, surface permeability and surface porosity of nanocoatings are the key parameters in controlling the corrosion behavior of nanocoatings.
the surface stress, surface modulus, surface porosities, permeability and the grain size are the intrinsic factors that affect the corrosion behavior of nanocomposite materials.
the corrosion resistance of the nanocomposite coating is a function of the mechanical and electrochemical properties of the coating and the electrolyte.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the corrosion behavior of nanocoatings is affected significantly by the intrinsic mechanical parameters of nanocoatings, and the mechano-electro-chemical approach is a useful tool to predict the corrosion behavior of the nanocomposite coating.

the proposed equations can be used as a tool to predict the corrosion failure of the nanocomposite coating and the results would be useful in the design and optimization of nanocoatings with desired corrosion properties.
the proposed equations can be used as a powerful tool for predicting corrosion failure and optimizing corrosion resistance of nanocoatings in a wide range of applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the mechanical parameters can have significant effects on the corrosion behavior of nanocomposite coating, and therefore, they should be considered in the design of nanocomposite materials for corrosion protection.
it is important to understand the influence of mechanical properties of nanocomposites on corrosion behavior in order to design and develop better nanocoatings.
the intrinsic mechanical properties of nanocoatings can be manipulated to achieve the desired level of corrosion protection.
